name: Attack on Titan
blurb: Isayama's dark fantasy of walled-in humans fighting giants, and the secret behind them
title: Attack on Titan Summary: Full Story and Ending Explained
description: Attack on Titan summary: the main characters, every arc from the fall of Wall Maria to the Rumbling, how the anime ends for Eren, Mikasa and Armin, and its themes.
h1: Attack on Titan: Summary, Characters and Ending Explained
answer: Attack on Titan is a Japanese anime series that aired from 2013 to 2023, adapted from Hajime Isayama's manga, which ran in Kodansha's Bessatsu Shōnen Magazine from 2009 to 2021. Wit Studio animated the first three seasons and MAPPA the final season. The last survivors of humanity live inside three enormous walls that keep out Titans, giant humanoid creatures that eat people. After a Titan breaks through and kills his mother, a boy named Eren Yeager joins the army to wipe the Titans out, and the story slowly turns into a war over who the Titans are and what lies beyond the walls.

head: Character
Who they are
rows: Eren Yeager
A hot-headed boy from the town of Shiganshina who swears to destroy every Titan
Mikasa Ackerman
Eren's adoptive sister, an exceptionally skilled soldier devoted to protecting him
Armin Arlert
Eren's childhood friend, physically weak but a brilliant strategist
Levi Ackerman
Captain in the Survey Corps, famed as humanity's strongest soldier
Erwin Smith
Commander of the Survey Corps, the unit that ventures outside the walls
Hange Zoë
A Survey Corps squad leader obsessed with studying Titans
Reiner Braun
A fellow cadet of Eren's, steady and dependable
Annie Leonhart
A quiet, aloof cadet with strong hand-to-hand skills
Historia Reiss
A cadet first known by another name, with a hidden family background
Zeke Yeager
A mysterious figure from outside the walls with a link to Eren's family

ol: Season 1 (2013): In the year 845 the Colossal Titan and the Armored Titan breach Wall Maria, and Eren watches a Titan eat his mother. Five years later Eren, Mikasa and Armin graduate as cadets. During a Titan attack on the town of Trost, Eren is swallowed and then emerges as a Titan himself: he can change into the Attack Titan and back. He uses the power to seal the breach, and the Survey Corps takes him into Levi's squad. On an expedition outside the walls a Female Titan wipes out much of the squad; Armin works out that she is their fellow cadet Annie, who is captured after a battle in the capital and seals herself in crystal.

Season 2 (2017): Titans appear inside Wall Rose. Reiner and Bertholdt Hoover confess that they are the Armored and Colossal Titans and kidnap Eren; the cadet Ymir turns out to be a Titan too. The Survey Corps wins Eren back, and in a moment of desperation Eren briefly commands ordinary Titans with a touch, a power known as the Coordinate.

Season 3 (2018–2019): The true royal family, the Reiss family, has secretly held the Founding Titan, which can alter the memories of people inside the walls. Rod Reiss captures Eren and tries to make his daughter Historia eat him to take the power; she refuses, Rod turns into a monstrous Titan and is killed, and Historia becomes queen. The Survey Corps retakes Shiganshina, but Erwin dies leading a suicide charge and Armin, near death, is saved by inheriting the Colossal Titan. In Eren's old basement they find his father Grisha's notes: humanity is not extinct. They are Eldians, a people able to turn into Titans, confined to the island of Paradis, while the nation of Marley across the sea holds the other Titan powers and plans to invade.

The Final Season, Parts 1 and 2 (2020–2022): Several years later the story moves to Marley, following Reiner and young Eldian soldiers. Eren, who has slipped in secretly, attacks the city of Liberio, kills Willy Tybur during a declaration of war against Paradis and takes the War Hammer Titan. Back home he breaks with his friends, works with his half-brother Zeke, and a faction called the Yeagerists takes over the island. When Marley strikes back, Eren makes contact with Zeke and reaches the Paths, a realm outside time where the first Titan, Ymir Fritz, lives. Instead of following Zeke's plan to stop Eldians having children, he starts the Rumbling: millions of colossal Titans hidden inside the walls march out to trample the world beyond Paradis.

The Final Chapters (2023): Former enemies join forces, Mikasa, Armin, Levi, Hange, Reiner, Annie and others, and fly to stop Eren, who has become a huge skeletal Titan. Hange gives her life to buy them time. In the final battle Levi kills Zeke, which halts the march, and Mikasa enters the giant Titan's mouth and kills Eren.

body: When Mikasa kills Eren, the power of the Titans disappears from the world. Everyone who had been turned into a Titan becomes human again, and Armin, Reiner and Annie lose their powers. By then the Rumbling has already killed around eighty percent of humanity.

In the Paths, Eren talks with Armin and admits the truth behind his choices. He had seen the future through the Attack Titan's power and acted to bring it about, even steering the Titan that ate his mother towards her so that Bertholdt would survive and the events that followed would happen. He let himself be stopped so that his friends would become the heroes who saved what was left of the world, and so that Paradis would be safe from attack for a time. He also confesses that he loves Mikasa and does not want to die. The finale suggests that Ymir Fritz, the first Titan, had stayed bound to the royal line out of love, and that seeing Mikasa end the life of the person she loved is what finally freed her.

Mikasa buries Eren under the tree on a hill near Shiganshina where they used to sit as children. Three years later Armin and his companions sail to Paradis for peace talks with Queen Historia. A bird wraps Mikasa's scarf back around her at the grave; the anime never says the bird is Eren, though many viewers read it that way, and birds have stood for freedom throughout the series. A sequence after the credits shows Mikasa visiting the grave into old age, Paradis growing into a modern city and then being bombed in a later war, and finally a boy and his dog finding the overgrown tree, which looks like the tree where Ymir first gained her power.

The meaning of the ending is debated. One reading is that it shows the cycle of hatred and war never truly ends, and the closing images suggest history repeating itself. Another sees it as a tragedy about freedom: Eren was free to choose but used that freedom to commit genocide. A third, more critical reading, common among manga readers, holds that the ending softens Eren's actions too much. In an interview with The New York Times, Isayama said a happy ending had seemed implausible to him and that he had to give it up.

ul: Freedom: Eren's longing to see beyond the walls turns into a willingness to destroy the world, and the story asks what freedom costs.
The cycle of hatred: Eldians and Marleyans each see the other as devils, and the series shows how revenge passes from one generation to the next.
Perspective: the Final Season moves the viewpoint to Marley, so the people Eren's friends fought as monsters become sympathetic characters.
Memory and history: the Founding Titan rewrites what people remember, and those who control history control how a nation sees itself.
Sacrifice and duty: soldiers such as Erwin and Hange give their lives for goals they will never see, and the series asks whether it was worth it.
Length: four seasons, 94 episodes counted together, including the two final specials released in March and November 2023 (about 24 minutes per regular episode).
Original: Hajime Isayama's manga, 139 chapters in 34 volumes (2009–2021); the anime follows it closely to the end, with a few scenes in the finale expanded.
Other versions: a two-part Japanese live-action film (2015) tells a different version of the early story.
Content advisory: very graphic violence, including people being eaten, and mass death, war crimes and genocide in later seasons.

check.q: What can Eren do that surprises everyone during the battle of Trost?
check.why: Eren is swallowed by a Titan and comes out as the Attack Titan, which he can turn into and out of.

check.q: What does Eren start in the Final Season?
options: A plan to stop Eldians having children
check.why: Eren rejects Zeke's plan and releases the Wall Titans to trample the world beyond Paradis.

check.q: Who kills Eren and ends the power of the Titans?
check.why: Mikasa enters the giant Titan's mouth and kills Eren, after which the Titans' power vanishes.

faq.q: Is the Attack on Titan anime ending different from the manga?
faq.a: The story is the same. The anime adds and expands a few moments in the finale, most noticeably Eren's conversation with Armin, which plays more emotionally, but the events and the final images match the manga.

faq.q: Why did Eren start the Rumbling?
faq.a: He wanted to protect Paradis from a world set on destroying it and had seen a future he felt bound to bring about. He also arranged to be stopped by his friends so they would be seen as heroes and the Eldians on the island would be safe for a time.

faq.q: In what order should I watch Attack on Titan?
faq.a: Watch in release order: Season 1, Season 2, Season 3 Parts 1 and 2, then The Final Season Parts 1 and 2 and the two-part Final Chapters special. The OVAs are optional side stories.
